data: First private orbital launch site: Rocket Lab's Electron from Mahia, New Zealand

Rocket Lab's own spaceport on the Mahia Peninsula, Hawke's Bay, with two pads, LC-1A and LC-1B. The complex opened on 26 September 2016; the first Electron attempt on 25 May 2017 (UTC) reached space but not orbit, and the first successful orbital launch followed on 21 January 2018. Facts from Wikipedia and the Rocket Lab Electron Payload User Guide; coordinates are LC-1A from Wikipedia, consistent with the guide's 39.262 S, 177.865 E.

On the Māhia Peninsula, on the east coast of New Zealand's North Island, Rocket Lab built the first private spaceport to host a successful orbital launch. It opened on 26 September 2016. The pads stand on a raised plateau about 104 m above the sea, with cliffs on three sides and a single access road. Electron's first flight, "It's a Test", left Pad A on 25 May 2017 and reached space but not orbit; the second, on 21 January 2018, put its satellites into orbit. Pad B flew its first mission on 28 February 2022. Rocket Lab's user guide gives a capacity of up to 120 launches a year. The company picked Māhia for its open sea to the east and sparse air traffic.
